claims.claim: Small-factor trial division establishes odd N and coprimality of the factor base.
If 0<X<N and X² is zero modulo N, gcd(X,N) is a proper factor.
Trial division decomposes the residue into the smooth part times T.
T=1 yields a valid relation with sign exponent zero.
A fixed number of independent trials gives a binomial relation count.
The count has mean MP and variance MP(1−P)<MP.
At least k dependencies after m+k outputs give failure probability at most 2^−k.
P(m,N)>=m^r/(r!N) for the stated even r.
An even r within one of sqrt(2 ln N/ln ln N) is admissible.
Choosing the prime cutoff downward achieves r=ln N/ln p_m+O(1/ln ln N).
The displayed expansion of ln p_m includes the rounding term theta.
Prime counting gives ln m=ln p_m−ln ln p_m+O(1/ln p_m).
claims.scope_note: PNT estimate from the preceding block is an explicit external input.

claims.claim: Substitution gives the stated theta-dependent expansion for ln m.

An integer M can be chosen so the expected number of outputs is at least 4m.
Elimination can be implemented in O(m³ poly(log N)) bit operations.
